reason: About 80% of the weight is bills adding an explicit right to equality to Basic Law: Human Dignity and Liberty or to the Nation-State Basic Law (rows 1, 3-10, 17, 20) - exactly the statement. Row 2 (conditioning the right to vote on military or national service, labeled away) is a sizable bill but is itself an equal-rights question: a voter who wants equality in the Basic Laws would oppose it, so it fits the same axis. Rows 13, 16, 19 (immigration Basic Law, infiltrators override, limiting freedom of occupation to citizens) are light and only loosely related; they do not change the meaning.
